title: What is a SIP phone? How it works and why businesses are switching
summary: A SIP phone lets your business make calls over the internet — more features, lower costs. Learn how SIP phones work and why cloud is the smarter choice.

## What is a SIP phone?


A **SIP phone** is a device — physical or software-based — that uses Session Initiation Protocol (SIP), the open communication standard, to set up and manage calls over an IP network, rather than a traditional copper phone line.


In plain terms: a SIP phone is a modern business phone that runs on your internet connection, not your wall jack.


## How a SIP phone works


### What SIP stands for — and why it matters


Session Initiation Protocol is an open, vendor-neutral standard for managing real-time voice and video sessions over IP networks. Think of SIP as the "handshake" between two phones: it handles the signaling — dialing, ringing, answering, hanging up — while the actual voice data travels separately over the network using a protocol called Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP).


Because SIP is an open standard, it works across hardware from different manufacturers and integrates with a wide range of[business phone systems](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/voip-phone/) and software platforms.


### The role of VoIP


SIP phones fall under the broader umbrella of voice over internet protocol (VoIP) technology. VoIP converts your voice into digital packets and transmits them over the internet. SIP is among the most widely used signaling protocols for VoIP calls. So while all SIP phones are VoIP phones, not all VoIP phones use SIP — some use proprietary protocols instead.


## Types of SIP phones


### SIP desk phones (hardware)


These look like traditional office phones — a handset, keypad, and screen — but connect to your network via ethernet or Wi-Fi instead of a phone line. They're a familiar option for employees who prefer a physical device on their desk. Many modern desk phones are SIP-compatible.


### SIP softphones


A softphone is software that turns your laptop, desktop, tablet, or smartphone into a SIP phone. There's no additional hardware needed to buy or maintain. Employees download an app, log in, and their device becomes a fully functional business phone. Softphones are a natural fit for hybrid and remote teams.


### SIP conference phones


These are purpose-built devices designed for group calls in meeting rooms. They connect to your SIP phone system like any other SIP endpoint, and can support many of the same system-level features — call routing, recording, and AI capabilities — as individual SIP phones.


## SIP phone vs. VoIP phone vs. IP phone — what's the difference?


These three terms are often used interchangeably, and the distinction matters:


Term What it means


**IP phone** Any phone that operates over an IP network


**VoIP phone** An IP phone that carries voice over an IP network using internet protocols


**SIP phone** A VoIP phone that uses SIP as its call-control protocol


SIP phone is the most specific term. When a vendor says their phone is "SIP-compatible," they mean it is designed to register with standard SIP servers — giving you flexibility to choose your own phone service provider or cloud system.


## Key features to look for in a SIP phone system


Not all SIP phone systems deliver the same capabilities. Here's what makes a real difference for small and midsize businesses:


- **Auto-attendant** — Routes inbound calls to the right person or department without a live receptionist.
- **Call queues** — Lines callers up and distributes calls to available agents efficiently.
- **Voicemail transcription** — Converts voicemails to text so you can read and prioritize messages faster.
- **Call recording** — Captures conversations for training, quality review, or compliance purposes.
- **Mobile and desktop apps** — Lets your team take business calls on a range of devices, whether in office, at home, or on the go.
- **CRM and app integrations** — Connects your phone system with tools in your business's tech stack.
- **Call analytics** — Gives you visibility into call volume, wait times, and agent performance.
- **AI features** — Surfaces call summaries, action items, and voicemail prioritization to help reduce manual follow-up — so your team spends less time on admin.


## Benefits of SIP phones for small businesses


Switching from a legacy phone system to a SIP phone system can deliver meaningful advantages:


**Lower costs.** You can minimize expensive hardware costs, separate phone lines, and carrier contracts. Because SIP runs over your existing internet connection, you're consolidating infrastructure rather than adding to it.


**Location flexibility.** Your team can make and receive business calls from virtually anywhere — the office, home, a co-working space, or the road. All they need is an internet connection and a compatible device.


**Easy to scale.** Adding a new employee? Add a user license, not new phone lines. Removing a departing employee is just as quick. SIP phone systems scale up and down with minimal IT overhead.


**More features, built in.** Many SIP-based cloud phone systems include features — such as call routing, shared lines, call queues, voicemail transcription — that may require costly add-ons or separate hardware on a traditional private branch exchange (PBX) system. For a deeper look at how cloud-based systems compare to on-premise PBX, check out[what a PBX phone system is](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/what-is-a-pbx-phone-system/) and how it differs from today's cloud alternatives.


**Works with existing hardware.** Many businesses keep their current SIP-compatible desk phones when they move to a cloud system. That means a faster, lower-cost transition.


## Security and compliance with SIP phone systems


This is one area where many SIP phone guides fall short — and where the choice of vendor can really matter. A SIP phone system is only as secure as the platform it runs on.


Key security capabilities to look for include:


- **End-to-end encryption** for calls and voicemail
- **E911 support** so emergency services can receive location information for callers


**Compliance-oriented controls**


- for regulated industries such as healthcare, financial services, and government
- **Role-based access controls** enabling admins to manage permissions without exposing sensitive settings
- **Uptime SLA** , a contractual commitment to availability when it matters most


Not all cloud SIP providers offer enterprise-grade security features. For businesses in regulated industries, verifying compliance controls before choosing a provider is a critical step.

## How to set up a SIP phone system


Getting started with a cloud SIP phone system is generally more straightforward than deploying traditional PBX hardware. Here's the general path:


1. **Choose your provider.** Compare plans based on call volume, the features your team needs, and whether you need international calling coverage.
2. **Select your devices.** Decide whether your team will use SIP desk phones, softphones (the app on their existing laptops and smartphones), or a mix of both.

4. **Configure call routing.** Set up your auto-attendant, call queues, business hours, and voicemail settings from the admin portal.
5. **Add users and go live.** Assign numbers, set permissions, and your team is ready to make and receive calls.

## Frequently asked questions


### What is a SIP phone?


A SIP phone is a device or software application that uses Session Initiation Protocol to manage calls over an IP network instead of traditional phone lines. SIP phones can be physical hardware (desk phones, conference phones) or software-based (softphones on a laptop or mobile device).


### What is the difference between a SIP phone and a VoIP phone?


VoIP is the broader technology category — it covers any voice call transmitted over the internet. SIP is among the most widely used protocols within VoIP for managing how calls are set up and ended. All SIP phones are VoIP phones, but not all VoIP phones use SIP; some use proprietary protocols from specific vendors.


### Do I need special hardware for a SIP phone?


No. While purpose-built SIP desk phones exist, you can use a SIP phone system entirely through a softphone app on your laptop, desktop, or smartphone. Many businesses use a combination of both — hardware phones at fixed desks and softphone apps for remote and mobile employees.


### Can I use a SIP phone without a PBX?


Yes. Modern cloud SIP phone systems replace the need for on-premise PBX hardware. Your "PBX" functions — call routing, auto-attendant, call queues, extensions — are managed in the cloud by your provider.


### Is Zoom Phone a SIP phone system?


Yes. Zoom Phone is a cloud-based SIP phone system that is compatible with SIP desk phones and also offers a softphone experience through the Zoom Workplace app. It supports number porting, bring your own carrier (BYOC) options, and standard SIP protocols.


### How secure are SIP phone calls?


Security depends on the provider. Look for a system that offers call encryption, E911 support, compliance controls for your industry, and a strong uptime SLA. Zoom Phone was designed with enterprise-grade security features and compliance controls.
